source: TSTD project (TA 7305-CAM), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំពោត" (Corn Cultivation Technical Manual), Section 3.a: Chemical (top-dress) fertilizer application, May 2012
text:
The manual gives a fertilizer application schedule for corn with four stages, each specifying timing, fertilizer type/amount, and placement method:

1) Before planting (about 15 days ahead): apply well-decomposed manure/compost, about 2 buckets per 1-meter-wide bed, worked into the soil before making the planting rows (this is the base compost application referenced in the land preparation step).

2) 7-10 days before planting: apply NPK fertilizer 20-20-15, about 5 grams per hole, placed in the single hole before sowing.

3) 7-10 days after planting: apply urea (46-0-0), about 1.5 grams per hole, sprinkled roughly 0.5-1 finger-width from the stem, on 2 sides per plant (the manual notes 1 bottle-cap/spoon measure holds about 1.5 grams, given as a practical dosing reference for farmers).

4) 28-30 days after planting: apply NPK 20-20-15 (mixed) again, about 5 grams per hole, sprinkled 1.5-2.5 finger-widths from the stem, on 1 side per plant.

5) 48-50 days after planting: apply NPK 20-20-15 plus potassium chloride (0-0-60) together, about 10 grams per hole, sprinkled 1.5-2.5 finger-widths from the stem, on 1 side per plant.

Between fertilizer applications, the manual instructs farmers to weed the field roughly on day 13, day 18, and day 35-37, before the final fertilizer application.
